describe: Films one scene of a capture file (fixtures/captures/<name>.json) for the capture CLI: ?capture=<name>&scene=<i>&cards=0|1, and record=1 to record the stage with tab capture.
The complete main-menu reel as a player-facing graphics test, with frame-rate summary and pacing chart.

The native client's control run: the graphics-test reel at 1280×720 with control plates read back from the canvas at each shot's middle; writes each scene's capture, visual presentation manifest and plates to throwaway/native-parity/. PARITY_SCENES=<map,…> films only those scenes.

The browser's half of the frame-rate comparison with the native client: the graphics-test reel without plates, on a production build at 1280×720, paced to the display; writes each scene's frame intervals, CPU and GPU times after the warm-up, and the in-game FPS counter's readings, to throwaway/perf/. FPS_SCENES=<map,…> picks the scenes.

The water scene: the water reel (fixtures/captures/water.json: close, tactical and low shots of the wetlands capture map's river) filmed by the graphics test with control plates and replayed by the native client from the same run. Each plate, in both clients, must show the simulation's river as water, bluer than its dry bank; the plates are written to the evidence in one sheet beside RedGPU's frozen stills for the side-by-side read.
Arrow and action cursor at native screen size over grass, road and fog; every badge and a moving pointer through the real presentation component.

Primitive 3D reproduction: asymmetric tank, facing-marked infantry, raised ground patch and box prop; pan/orbit/zoom, pick and reset. Includes player-low picture checks for the frame, geometry and river compositions.
Authoritative terrain and obstacles: ridge, slope threshold, forest volume, road, a river with a bridge, low/tall/thin walls; click probes the exported surface; overlay toggles.
Matched local terrain scaling at three zooms, with horizontal and elevated remote geometry; production frame measurements and pictures.
One authority in a worker: real tick commands with an ordered ack log, pause/step/reset, withheld consumer credit and an in-thread replay/parity check.

Routing and group intent: shortest vs fastest routes, group destinations, friendly traffic, a wall injected at tick 150, route-blocked destinations; select/drag, right-click, double right-click, Shift queue, S stop.

A river as one distance: a meander that widens from the 12 m minimum to a 30 m stretch, carved into the ground with gentle banks, crossed by a country road's bridge, a dirt track beside it and a wood over one bank. A squad and a tank on the road cross by its bridge; sent into the water, their route is blocked. The traversable-ground toggle shows what blocks and how the banks' facets shade.

Own sensors and shared identification: a scripted red tank tours thin forest, deep forest, the ridge's far side and a building's shadow; ground fog; per-unit own-sensor lists; labelled side-view switch. Includes contact UNKNOWN labels, red glow, overlay isolation and captions.

Physical flight and swept collision: gravity arcs, a fast bullet leading a thin sliding target, dodge after launch, a hill crest blocking direct fire while the indirect high arc clears it, and bodies crossing a round's line between ticks.

Independent weapons: a rifle squad (rifles + grenade launcher) and a tank (cannon with AP/HE + HMG) against a red tank that ducks behind a wall and a hidden squad firing from behind a low wall; per-mount aim/reload bars and action reasons; attack identified/contact/ground, attack-move, engagement policy switch.

Consequences of physical fire: HE into an exposed squad and a forest squad side by side, a friendly squad close enough to share the blast, a red tank destroyed in a walled passage whose wreck reroutes a supply truck, fallen soldiers that stay, and each squad's suppression in its info panel. Includes one browser check that drawn debris follows a destroyed hull.

Test helicopters hovering at cruise height, each with its ground marker and drop line: ?variant=hover (default) over open ground, a jeep on the road below for scale (its rotors turn, its shadow lies on the ground off to the side, nothing under it raises dust or rolls; selected, its marker and line take the selection's colour; ordered away with Space held, its ghost flies at cruise height); ?variant=roof over a house, the line cut by the roof, an identified enemy one over the field beyond; ?variant=fog an enemy one seen over the ground the house hides from blue's jeep; ?variant=apache the AH-64E on its real art, its chin gun firing down at an enemy tank on the road with its flash at the barrel's tip; ?variant=lost an enemy one blue's jeep loses behind the shop it stands against, its last sighting a red sign facing the camera at its height, with a thin stem to the ground under it.

A test helicopter, one hit from death, flies across the field past a gun jeep, trailing smoke, and is shot down: it falls on in a spinning arc, nose down, keeping its momentum, bursts where it strikes the ground and leaves its wreck there. It never vanishes in mid-air or brews up like a ground hull.

An F-16 flies across the air field, over the village, the tower and the wood, beside an enemy Mi-8 and J-10: blue's fog never clears and it never identifies the T-72 in the village, though the jet identifies both enemy aircraft; it stays inside the map at the air layer's height.

Layered air defence from red's side: ?variant=helicopter, an Apache and a Mi-8 fly in: the Buk and the short gun engage them, the long S-300 never does; ?variant=jet, an F-16 flies in: the short gun, the Buk and the S-300 fire at it, and the short gun the tower hides from it is direct fire like any other, with no air-only sight rule.

A 2v2 jet fight on air-jet, directed by attack orders, grows when a third blue jet joins: the selected jet carries the DOGFIGHT card, and an explicit move takes it out of the fight while its wingman keeps fighting. The trace and shot show the turning paths.

Paid jet ingress on air-jet: both purchases debit immediately; the delay has no unit or enemy draw; an approach AirTransit streaks over the render margin, then the jet arrives on blue’s back edge at cruise height heading in; after fuel burn it withdraws through the nearest back edge and is refunded.

Air-ground passes on the 3 km air-jet field with the roster's loadouts: an F-15E dives and releases its bombs; an F-16 makes a nose-on gun pass; an EA-18G's attack on the Buk's radar contact is accepted and it fires. The height trace, passes strip and full-field frame with the jet-only fog are for review.

Air-jet survivability: a Buk fires decoyable 290 m/s proximity-fused missiles at an F-16, which spends a flare, and at an Apache without flares, which is shot down. The shot shows the missile and flare tracks together.

Every faction's short, medium and long air defence, SEAD jet and other fixed-wing aircraft as the roster's cards list them, in a matrix beside the battle that parks each of those types on the air field, with a contact sheet of their runtime models. Includes the resolved air-war records panel.

Air-jet HUD: a jet has no ground marker or drop line while the Apache has both; the jet card shows fuel and flares; Space reveals the jet order ghost card; the radar contact card keeps its bearing and range.

The air alarm: a J-10 flies into the view of blue's marine squad, and blue hears one alarm and the jet's approach; while it stays seen no second alarm sounds; it flies off out of sight and back, a new episode, and the alarm sounds once more.

Passenger transport: squads board an APC and scout car from both directions, ride hidden, and drive past an enemy and an objective; their carriers' Seats rows and stacked rider cards. The controls variant drives the player's own controls: right-click boarding both ways under the board cursor, a squad refused for want of seats, its deck card while aboard, U then a click with the unload mark on its order line, and U twice. The heli variant: a transport helicopter flies to a squad, sinks to a low hover, the squad boards, it flies on and sinks again at its goal, and the squad gets out onto the ground beneath it.

Buildings as fighting positions: the closest eligible blue squad enters a building while selected companions gather outside; direct entry admits one squad whole, enter and leave on a timer, and fire outward from perimeter slots while red's rounds hit occupants or the walls; a red squad behind the building is seen only once occupants stand on that facade, and the occupants are HIDDEN until it walks up close enough to see them; red's tank brings the building down into a lower, impassable ruin and survivors escape pinned. Includes delayed admission, queued cursor, refusal callout and edge-readout cursor checks.

Recovery with finite stock: a supply truck sets up (3 s) and serves a damaged tank, an AT team short of missiles and a rifle squad with casualties; moving units wait; stock falls and never regrows; an empty truck leaves its neighbours waiting for stock; relocation. Includes the service-ready deployment text.

The ground layer as each side learns it: two tanks race east, one through an authored crater field (craters slow vehicles slightly, never their plan); two tanks shell a red squad in craters and one in the open; a squad walks the field; a flat cell view of the observed side's learned craters, scorch, tracks and trampling, rebuilt from its ground patches, with a side switch and the patch stream readout.

Info panel workbench: every info panel the battle can draw (own units of every type, each weapon situation and state row, the busiest panels, identified enemies, last sightings, heard reports, selected and far-zoom), through the battle's own panel component on a plain ground and over grass; ?scale= zooms.

UI gallery: every interface piece the panel workbench and cursor lab do not draw (top status strip in each phase, the end-of-match report at 1v1, 2v2, 5v5 and watched, battle clock, reinforcements picker, objective markers, range ruler, refused order, frame rate, captions, pause menu, loading and its failure), each in fixed states through the game's own components; ?shot= draws one. Its scene also pins every main-menu page.

Weapon readouts: each unit's info panel with a row per weapon (rounds left, ∞ unlimited; aim and reload rings round the weapon's icon while they run; the guidance mark) and its states; the army deck's card keeps a unit's whole panel when zoomed out, and clicking a card already selected centres the camera on its unit; the command bar exposes the selection's actions (X attack-move, G attack ground, Backspace stop, F fire policy).

Camera clearance: scripted camera trajectories round a wall, a tower, a corner of two tall slabs, a courtyard block and a concave compound (the generator's templates). Watch from outside, with the eye path asked for (amber, red inside a building's clearance) beside the eye path drawn (cyan), or ride the camera as the viewport flies it; a switch makes blue see the courtyard block collapse.

Every building template of the installed art library on flat ground, in rows by category at its real size, each labelled with its id, drawn through the frame's own buildings path with no battle. ?set= or ?category= narrows it, ?tier=0..3 draws every building at one detail tier, ?state=ruin|gutted draws the templates that end in that state as a side that saw them destroyed knows them (a low template collapses to a ruin, a tall one stands gutted; the others are left out), and ?station= with ?at=<template id> opens on a station: all, row, fit, close (30 m), tactical (65 m), wide (250 m), or transition-1..3 (where the template changes to that tier). The scene writes its per-tier contact sheets only when CITY_LINEUP_SHEETS=1.

Buildings destroyed in a battle, drawn as each side knows them: on the camera lab's map, HE bursts bring a five-floor U block down to remains and gut a twenty-floor tower, which stands. Blue's squad watches both and draws the block's ruin and the tower's burnt shell; red's stands behind two slabs and draws both intact until its scripted walk takes it round them; a labelled side-view switch. The camera's obstacles, the fog's occluders and the smoke over a destroyed building follow the same knowledge. Includes the building-fall rendering check.

What a facade material can say beyond opaque, on the facade lab's kit with no battle on it: a grille and a perforated sheet as fence panels (cutouts: there or not texel by texel, in colour, depth and shadow); free-standing panes of glass, each half across the next (blended over what is behind them, unsorted); and a block three bays wide and three floors high with a pane and a room behind every window and shopfront (a cell of the interior atlas, unlit, chosen by where the window stands). Stations cut the camera to each from 25 m, the default tactical camera and 250 m; ?blocks= stands a field of blocks behind (a dense view for the paired cost), ?fog=1 ends an eye's sight across each station, ?azimuth= and ?sun= turn and raise the sun, ?order=reversed hands the frame the same modules in the opposite order.

A battle on the street test map through the production controls, readouts and pause menu: blue starts west of the street, red holds it under the encounter's defender policy (its rifle squads garrison the three buildings). ?watch plays the encounter where blue's start is ordered onto the street at once, under a free camera; ?seed= sets the seed. The browser scenes judge the battle view here.

The street battle watched: blue's start ordered onto the street at once, the camera free. The scene takes the whole-battle frames at a fixed tick (BATTLE_TICK), and checks that ground past the playable area's edge is always unseen, and the dim white border that marks the area.

A prepared battle: what the skirmish lobby's Deploy starts. ?type=open|mixed|metro, ?size=small|medium|large|xl and ?seed= choose a generated map; ?blue= and ?red= carry ordered controller codes, while ?blue_faction= and ?red_faction= name the two side factions; ?battle= is the battle's seed; ?replay=saved watches a saved replay. A preparation worker generates the map and fields both factions on its skirmish sites; a loading screen covers the wait and a refusal names its stage. Its buildings are drawn from the template art library: kit modules where a template has art, a stand-in box where it has none yet. Its scene also checks that a lobby whose generation is exhausted or stalled shows no map and keeps Deploy shut. Includes generated-town still-camera, multipart orientation and replacement allocation checks.

Final player journey: zoom into preparation, recruit units, preview and face placement ghosts, start the match, move and face a unit, hold Space for its order marker, and pin the journey's screenshots and GPU diagnostics.

A 2v2 team battle from its link, you and one AI ally against two AI: allies drawn apart from your units (pale ice panels, a broken ring when selected, x-ray), at default and far zoom; selecting an ally opens its panel read-only with its owner line and offers no order; a box over both armies selects only yours.
A 2v2 team battle: you hold the far objective with one squad, and under pressure your AI ally sends a detachment, not its whole force, toward your objective.

The benchmark (the one frame-cost measure), reached from the menu: city contact, the simulation's central city-arena-2 stress on Metro XL seed 4, warm-started to contact, a keyframed camera tour through strategic, pan, zoom, ground, combined and return, then the results screen and JSON report. The scene runs the 60 s short run and writes the frame-cost row.

Synthetic stress battle for the scale verdict: 100 units a side, waves, reserves, a speculative-fire burst, an optional late state with the full roster fallen (800 soldiers and 100 wrecks), with live frame, heap, GPU and load telemetry. Set ENDURANCE_S for a longer real-time run.

Sight-light fog over the street test map: blue's eyes cut by the terrain and the buildings it knows, per pixel; the live frame or a seen/unseen mask; agreement with the simulation's 8 m sweep, the GPU sight shape against Rust's vectors, a turned turret and a garrison's eyes.
Projectile review with the fog-lit street close fight and range-limit rifle, HMG, AP, HE, ATGM, grenade and autocannon lanes; gameplay flight, unlimited reserves and nonlethal rounds.

Model workbench: drop a GLB (or /labs/workbench?bundle=name) to see validator findings and the production render — named views, a 1.8 m figure, the simulation hit box, socket gizmos, clip and phase scrubber, pose inputs, a feed replay through the pose driver, stats, sheets and the impostor bake.

How unseen looks: the fixture's named fog styles over the street test map under a 16:00 sun, every number live on sliders with a copyable presentation.fog block; roofs and canopy tops above the eyes; contact glyphs (red through the middle, hatched, a last sighting ringed pale).

The battle's sound: a scripted eight-second firefight rendered offline through the battle's audio graph (rifles, a tank driving and traversing, AP, HE, HMG, a ricochet, a guided missile, a burning wreck, the countryside, and unseen enemies heard only as cues); play it here, and the scene measures levels per bus, clipping and onsets against the visual events.

The lobby's map picture alone: real admitted maps for 1v1, 3v4 and 5v5 at S, M, L and XL, each through the lobby's preview controller at lobby size, with the refusal a pairing below a size's floor gets; ?cell=3v4-large draws one.

The skirmish lobby at /: an order of battle over real admitted map previews. Its scene covers the 1v1 default, the 3v3 and 5v5 presets, 3v4 and 2v3 by Add and Delete, taking another Blue seat, the size floor, a preview on opening and on each map change, Reroll, a hidden retry, a map that cannot be made, and Deploy starting the previewed map, and shoots each state at 1280×720 and 1920×1080.
Local generation and numerical validation tuning: searchable controls, authoritative plan, exact save review, retained inputs and seed samples.
Scenario authoring and play: place units, download a self-contained package, upload that package into the normal battle worker, and boot the playable world.
